title: Flash load after halting a running target fails with IPSR=3 or flash init timeout
symptoms: target was not halted as expected after calling flash algorithm routine (IPSR=3)
flash init timed out
cause: Flash algorithms assume the core starts from a reset state. Halting a running application and then loading leaves its MPU, stack limits and other state active, so the RAM-resident algorithm faults or never finishes.
fix: Reset the target and halt it before programming: use 'reset halt' in the commander, or 'monitor reset halt' before 'load' in gdb. 'pyocd flash' already does this by default.

title: J-Link SWO reader thread dies with IndexError: invalid index
symptoms: IndexError: invalid index
cause: The J-Link probe's SWO read passed the byte count straight to pylink, even when no data was available (count 0), which pylink cannot turn into a buffer.
fix: Skip the read when the available byte count is zero. Fixed in pyOCD by a follow-up change; update pyOCD. A monkey patch returning an empty list for a zero count works meanwhile.

title: pyocd hangs forever on first connect with hidapi backend on Windows
cause: The hidapi USB backend on Windows had no read timeout, so a read that never completes blocks the process and it cannot exit.
fix: Update to a pyOCD release that includes the fix for the hidapi read timeout (change #2011).

title: CMSIS-DAP v2 probe without USB serial number is listed but 'not found' when opening
symptoms: Probe NKBA2RU557ZLCOPTYPWHIX3IZUQ5ZH7B not found [__main__]
cause: A probe with no USB serial string gets a generated unique ID in the probe list, but the open path compared that ID against the real (missing) serial number and failed to match the device.
fix: Use a pyOCD version containing the fix for serial-less CMSIS-DAP v2 probes (change #2007), which the reporter confirmed.

title: RTT up channel bytes_available raises AttributeError on 'target'
symptoms: 'GenericRTTUpChannel' object has no attribute 'target'
cause: Typo in the RTT channel code: it used an attribute named target where the object stores it as _target.
fix: Fixed upstream; use a pyOCD release that includes the correction.

title: fast_program with smart_flash leaves parts of erased sectors blank (silent data loss)
symptoms: Erased 32768 bytes (2 sectors), programmed 8192 bytes (2 pages), skipped 57344 bytes (14 pages)
cause: With fast_program and smart_flash, pages whose CRC matched were marked unchanged and the step that forces all pages of a dirty sector to be rewritten was skipped. Sector erase then wiped pages that were never reprogrammed, on devices whose sectors are larger than pages.
fix: Update pyOCD to a release including change #2004. Until then avoid -O fast_program=true together with smart_flash on parts with sector size larger than page size, and verify read-back.

title: J-Link open by serial number fails with 'No emulator with serial number found'
symptoms: No emulator with serial number <SN> found.
cause: With jlink.non_interactive enabled (default), pyOCD disables dialog boxes in the J-Link DLL before opening the probe, and with some DLL versions this breaks opening by serial number.
fix: Set 'jlink.non_interactive: false' in pyocd.yaml as a workaround, or upgrade to a pyOCD release with the reordering fix (change #1927).

title: load --cbuild-run: post-load hardware reset breaks SWD without ResetHardware sequence
symptoms: Error while running debug sequence 'DebugCoreStop' (core Cortex-M0+): SWD/JTAG communication failure (No ACK) [cbuild_run]
cause: From 0.42.0 the load command defaults the post-reset to a hardware reset when the cbuild-run file has no load-setup section. On devices whose pack lacks a custom ResetHardware sequence, the plain nRESET also resets the debug port and reconnecting fails, even though programming succeeded.
fix: Upgrade to 0.44.1, which reworked post-reset handling. Meanwhile pass '-O load.post_reset=sysresetreq' to pyocd load.

title: pyocd pack install with a name prefix finds no devices on Python 3.14
symptoms: W No matching devices
cause: A change in how prefix matching worked broke under Python 3.14; the same command works on Python 3.13 and a full part name always works.
fix: Use Python 3.13 or earlier, install the full part number, or upgrade to a pyOCD release containing change #1993.

title: Pack defines DHCSR_Addr in <debugvars>: 'attempt to modify read-only variable'
symptoms: RuntimeError: attempt to modify read-only variable 'DHCSR_Addr'
cause: Variables declared in a pack's global debugvars are read-only. From 0.44.0 the default debug sequences (such as DebugCoreStart) are used when a pack lacks its own, and they declared locals with the same names, which clashed with the pack's global.
fix: Upgrade to 0.44.1, where the locals in the default sequences carry a '__' prefix. Alternatively avoid reusing the register-address variable names as global debugvars.

title: J-Link fails to open with 'No emulator with serial number' on newer J-Link DLLs
symptoms: pylink.errors.JLinkException: No emulator with serial number 1064xxxxx2 found.
cause: A known incompatibility between pylink and J-Link DLL versions above about 9.12: opening by serial number fails, apparently after dialog boxes are disabled or several JLink instances are created.
fix: Use a pyOCD build containing change #1927 (reorders disabling of dialog boxes). On Windows some dialog boxes may then reappear.

title: pack install silently does nothing when index version differs from vendor pdsc
symptoms: Downloading packs (press Control-C to cancel):
cause: The pack listed in the index has a newer version than what the vendor's pdsc or the download actually provides, so the expected version never appears locally and the part stays 'not installed'.
fix: Workaround reported: rename the locally downloaded pdsc/pack to the expected version, or use --pack with the pack file. Retrying after the index was corrected also worked for some packs.

title: CMSIS-DAP v2 bulk: stray zero byte after transfers sized as multiple of endpoint size
cause: pyOCD's USB backend appends a dummy zero byte to bulk writes whose length is a multiple of wMaxPacketSize but shorter than the DAP packet size, to terminate the transfer. Probe firmware that treats every byte as data sees a bogus one-byte packet.
fix: The extra byte was introduced on purpose to end the USB transfer; a later change (#1882) altered it so it no longer shows up in the command stream. Update pyOCD or make probe firmware tolerate it.

title: pip install pyocd fails building hidapi on Python 3.14
symptoms: Building wheel for hidapi (pyproject.toml) ... error
cause: hidapi had no wheel for Python 3.14 so pip compiled it and needed a C++ build toolchain; libusb-package also lacked a 3.14 wheel at first.
fix: Use a recent pyOCD: hidapi 0.15.0 and a newer libusb-package ship Python 3.14 wheels, so install works without a compiler. Otherwise use an older Python.

title: Flashing AIR001 fails with Memory transfer fault (write) after 0.36.0
symptoms: C Memory transfer fault (write) @ 0x20001000-0x2000107f [__main__]
cause: The built-in flash algorithm placed its data buffer at a RAM address that was wrong for the target when double buffering was not in use; this affected many internal targets, not only AIR001.
fix: Upgrade to a release containing change #1898 (generic fix for all internal targets). Workaround was moving the begin_data address in the target file to RAM start plus 0x270.

title: EFR32BG22 pack: 'Memory regions must have a non-zero length'
symptoms: C Error: Memory regions must have a non-zero length. [__main__]
cause: The Silicon Labs DFP 2025.6.2 contained a faulty memory region definition and a flash loader problem.
fix: Install the DFP version 2025.12.1 or later, which fixes both. Passing -O adi.v5.max_invalid_ap_count=0 helped with non-responsive APs during enumeration.

title: CMSIS-DAP v1 probe 'not found' on Windows/macOS after upgrading from 0.36 to 0.40
cause: A rework of the hidapi backend in 0.40 mishandled report sizes for some HID-based CMSIS-DAP v1 probes.
fix: Use a release including change #1854, which fixes the hidapi backend by reading the HID report descriptor.

title: pyocd load fails on boards without nRESET wired (3-wire SWD) since 0.40
cause: From 0.40.0 the load command always performs a hardware reset via nSRST afterwards, which does nothing useful or breaks SWD when the reset pin is not connected.
fix: Workaround: 'pyocd load --no-reset ...' followed by 'pyocd reset'. The fixed releases add pre-reset and post-reset session options and restore the old default behaviour.

title: Low-speed USB CMSIS-DAP v1 probe fails on Windows: packet size error then 'already open'
symptoms: DAP_Info Packet Size 64 exceeds endpoint wMaxPacketSize 8
Error: already open
cause: On Windows and Linux the hidapi backend derives HID report size from the endpoint size (8 bytes for a low-speed device) instead of the HID report descriptor, which says 64. The failed open leaves the device open so a retry errors.
fix: Windows and macOS were fixed by the hidapi backend rework (change #1854). Linux uses the pyusb backend and remained broken in the thread.

title: Cannot write STM32F1 option bytes: no memory region defined at 0x1ffff800
symptoms: no memory region defined for address 0x1ffff800
cause: The pack lists the option-byte flash algorithm as non-default, so pyOCD does not create a flash region for it.
fix: Add the region yourself in a pyocd_user.py script: load the unprocessed pack algorithms and add a FlashRegion for the option-byte algorithm to the memory map.

title: Semihosting read of zero bytes crashes the gdbserver with TypeError
symptoms: TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()
cause: The semihosting console read computed the result from the data length before checking that any data was returned.
fix: Fixed in change #1811; update pyOCD.

title: cbuild-run load rejects IAR .out ELF files
cause: CMSIS-Toolbox names IAR output with the .out extension, which pyOCD's file programmer did not recognise as ELF.
fix: Fixed in a pyOCD commit that adds the extension; use a release containing it.

title: Connect fails on devices with an extra core not described in the debug topology
symptoms: C Error: <APv1Address@0x1d6da825540 #1 dp=0> [__main__]
cause: Discovery found a second AP/core that the pack's topology does not list, and creating it raised an exception during session open.
fix: Fixed in later releases (changes #1865 and follow-ups): unknown cores are not added to the core list, but remain reachable through direct AP access.

title: CMSIS-DAP bulk SWO: 'read thread exited unexpectedly'
symptoms: pyocd.core.exceptions.ProbeError: Probe 0123456789 read thread exited unexpectedly
cause: A flag marking the SWO thread as finished stayed set when the USB interface was closed and reused, so the reader reported failure although the thread was running.
fix: Fixed by changes #1755 and #1824; update pyOCD.

title: RTT: 'Control block not found' although the SEGGER RTT ID is in RAM
symptoms: C Control block not found [__main__]
cause: pyOCD's RTT search could only find a control block aligned to 16 or 32 bytes.
fix: Compile the firmware with SEGGER_RTT_CB_ALIGN set to 16 or 32; a search fix was merged in change #1730.

title: STM32H7 flash corrupted occasionally with double buffering
cause: Double-buffered flash programming can stall on the bus of devices with strict timing such as STM32H7, leaving pages partly written (rest 0xFF) without any error.
fix: Upgrade to 0.37 or later, which disables double buffering by default; a built-in H743 target also worked better than the pack loader. Always verify flash after programming.

title: Executable built with PyInstaller reports 'No connected debug probes'
symptoms: No connected debug probes
cause: PyInstaller does not bundle pyOCD's probe plugins (entry points), the libusb DLL and native extensions by default, so no probe backend loads.
fix: Collect the 'pyocd.probe' and 'pyocd.rtos' entry points, pyocd and pylink package data and the libusb DLL in the .spec file. Releases from 0.38.0 provide prebuilt binaries.

title: pyocd list shows no probe with Python 3.12 and 0.36.0 on Windows
symptoms: No available debug probes are connected
cause: libusb-package had no wheel for Python 3.12, so pip tried to build it and, without Visual Studio, installed it without libusb-1.0.dll.
fix: Place libusb-1.0.dll (from the libusb releases) in a location on the search path such as C:\Windows\System32, or use a Python/libusb-package combination that has a wheel.

title: RTT control block not found when its ID string straddles a 32-byte boundary
symptoms: C Control block not found [__main__]
cause: The control block search code read memory in chunks and missed an ID string that crossed a chunk boundary.
fix: Workaround: start the search 16 bytes later (change -a address by 0x10) or force 16-byte alignment of the block. Fixed by change #1669 in a later release.

title: Erase/load fails with IPSR=3 after upgrading to 0.36 on Cortex-M0 devices
symptoms: W T bit in XPSR is invalid; the vector table may be invalid or corrupt [cortex_m]
C target was not halted as expected after calling flash algorithm routine (IPSR=3) [__main__]
cause: The flash algorithm was started with the Thumb bit clear in xPSR, which faults on Cortex-M.
fix: Fixed in 0.37.0 by writing the Thumb bit before running algorithm functions; upgrade.

title: HC32F460 flash fails with IPSR=3 after 0.35: wrong target name used with the pack
symptoms: C target was not halted as expected after calling flash algorithm routine (IPSR=3) [__main__]
cause: The user selected the part name hc32f460jeua; the valid target names are hc32f460xc and hc32f460xe. Also, 0.35 changed flash algorithm RAM layout and 0.34 might have skipped programming through smart flash.
fix: Use -t hc32f460xe (or xc). Pass -Osmart_flash=0 to force programming when comparing versions.

title: HC32L130 built-in target cannot write above 32 KB
symptoms: W Failed to add data chunk: no memory region defined for address 0x00008000 [file_programmer]
cause: The built-in memory map for the part covered only the first 32 KB of flash.
fix: Fixed by change #1590; use a release containing it, or use the vendor pack with the specific part name.

title: XDS110-based LaunchPad: USB read timeout during flash
symptoms: usb.core.USBTimeoutError: [Errno 110] Operation timed out
cause: The probe firmware does not cope with several outstanding CMSIS-DAP requests; reads time out.
fix: Add -Ocmsis_dap.limit_packets to prevent multiple outstanding commands. Note: reflashing an identical image is skipped by smart flash; use -Osmart_flash=0 to force programming.

title: nRF91 auto-unlock fails with a probe that has no nRESET line
cause: Unlocking this SiP revision requires pin reset from the probe, which a probe offering only SWCLK and SWDIO cannot provide.
fix: Unlock the device and then power cycle it before reconnecting, or use a probe wired to nRST.

title: pyocd list shows target n/a for standalone ST-Link
cause: Automatic target detection only works for on-board probes whose firmware reports the board type; a standalone ST-Link cannot identify the MCU.
fix: Map the probe unique ID to a target in pyocd.yaml under 'probes:' with 'target_override', or pass -t.

title: -Ocmsis_dap.prefer_v1 ignored by load/gdbserver; v2 open fails on Windows
symptoms: C Error: Operation not supported or unimplemented on this platform [__main__]
cause: Probe enumeration reads cmsis_dap.prefer_v1 before command-line options are parsed, so it is ignored. The underlying v2 failure was a libusb bug: interface numbers of 10 or higher are mis-parsed on Windows.
fix: Renumber the probe's USB interfaces so the v2 interface is below 10, or use a different libusb build. Use a config file for prefer_v1.

title: RTT 'Control block not found' after upgrading from 0.34.3 to 0.35
symptoms: C Control block not found [__main__]
cause: The search compared a full 16-byte padded ID, so a block whose ID string is followed by non-zero bytes ('SEGGER RTT' is shorter than 16) was missed.
fix: Fix the search to match only the real ID length; a local fix worked and a maintainer asked for a pull request. Downgrading to 0.34.3 is a stop-gap.

title: SPSDK breaks with pyOCD 0.35.0: DPConnector missing 'dp' argument
symptoms: Entering into ISP mode failed: DPConnector.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'dp'
cause: pyOCD 0.35.0 changed the DPConnector constructor signature, breaking callers that passed only the probe.
fix: The maintainer planned to revert the API change; alternatively pass the debug port explicitly as second argument.

title: i.MX RT685 pack: debug sequence parse error on 'U' integer suffix and no cores discovered
symptoms: Unexpected token Token('IDENT', 'U') at line 3, column 34.
C No cores were discovered! [__main__]
cause: The NXP pack uses C-style 'U' suffixes in debug sequence literals, which pyOCD's parser rejected. Later, DebugPortStart was bound to a named core, so pyOCD did not run it and the debug AP stayed locked.
fix: Parser fix in change #1548. For the second problem remove Pname="cm33" from the DebugPortStart sequence in the pdsc (use an expanded pack directory) until core-specific port sequences are supported. Use the .FLM from the pack, not the .cfx.

title: Semihosting binary file write raises UnicodeDecodeError
symptoms: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x81 in position 0: invalid start byte
cause: The semihosting layer decodes target data as UTF-8 text even when the file is opened as binary.
fix: Maintainers agreed the string helper must return bytes and only text-mode files should be encoded or decoded; also let the target open files in binary mode. Check for a release with the change.

title: Board ID maps to a target name pyOCD does not recognise (stm32h745zihx)
symptoms: Target type stm32h745zihx not recognized. Use 'pyocd list --targets' to see currently available target types.
cause: The board ID table assigned a wrong target name for the discovery board.
fix: Pass the right target explicitly, e.g. -t STM32H745XIHx. Flash loading then still faulted (IPSR=3) in this thread, left open.

title: 'Target type ... not recognized' for an STM32 board; pack not installed
symptoms: Target type stm32f407vgtx not recognized. Use 'pyocd list --targets' to see currently available target types.
cause: The target comes from a CMSIS-Pack that was not installed. Errors from 'pyocd pack update' about vendor servers are expected, and large packs download slowly without progress.
fix: Run 'pyocd pack update' then 'pyocd pack install <part>' and wait for the download to finish.

title: pyocd pack install finds no devices; pack update produces XML warnings
symptoms: W No matching devices. Please make sure the pack index is up to date. [pack_cmd]
cause: Updating the index with many concurrent requests triggered server protection at Keil and NXP, leaving corrupted descriptors.
fix: Upgrade cmsis-pack-manager to 0.5.2 or later and run 'pyocd pack update --clean'. Some remaining download errors for broken vendor entries are normal.

title: reset_and_halt then resume logs 'cannot resume: target not halted'
cause: The message came from the automatic resume on disconnect, not from the resume call, so the script behaved correctly.
fix: Pass resume_on_disconnect=False; the message was reworded in change #1487.

title: PyInstaller build cannot load cmsis_pack_manager native library or plugins
symptoms: OSError: cannot load library
cause: The frozen app lacks the native cmsis_pack_manager module and libusb library, so plugin loading fails and no probe is found.
fix: Add the libusb DLL and the cmsis_pack_manager native module as data/binaries in the PyInstaller spec (see the pyOCD discussion on binary builds).

title: Renesas RA pack: flash algorithm not found, target type not recognized
symptoms: KeyError: "There is no item named 'Flash/RA2A1_256K.FLM' in the archive"
cause: The Renesas pack stores its pdsc in a subdirectory; pyOCD found it but resolved algorithm paths relative to the archive root.
fix: Fixed by change #1461 which supports the non-standard layout; upgrade.

title: LPC54 devices use the LPC55 unlock sequence and cannot reset and halt
symptoms: W had to forcibly halt core after reset [target_lpc5500]
cause: The LPC5500 family regular expression also matched LPC54xx parts, so the LPC55 debug-mailbox unlock sequence ran on a chip that has no such access port.
fix: Fixed by change #1440; upgrade.

title: File path containing '@' breaks flash/load
symptoms: invalid literal for int() with base 0:
cause: The load command treats '@<address>' after a file name as a load address, so a directory name with '@' is cut apart.
fix: The maintainer planned to check whether the full argument is an existing file first. Meanwhile avoid '@' in paths or use --base-address.

title: pip install from git develop fails in setuptools_scm with GPG signature
symptoms: Getting requirements to build wheel ... error
cause: setuptools_scm 6.4.2 chokes on signed commits when git log shows signatures; fixed in 6.4.3.
fix: Run 'git config --global log.showSignature false' before installing, or upgrade setuptools_scm.

title: WCH-Link CMSIS-DAP probe not detected
symptoms: No available debug probes are connected
cause: pyOCD matches probes by name strings rather than VID/PID, and this WCH-Link answers string descriptor requests incorrectly in some conditions.
fix: Matching by VID/PID pair was added in change #1399; upgrade. Workaround on Linux: use the hidapi backend (PYOCD_USB_BACKEND=hidapiusb) after allowing the product name.

title: gdbserver answers an unsupported qXfer request with a malformed '9+' reply
cause: pyOCD only handled target.xml for qXfer feature reads and returned a garbled packet for other files such as arm-m-profile.xml, leaving the client waiting.
fix: Fixed by change #1414; update pyOCD.

title: pyocd reset with hardware reset does nothing on K64F
cause: The hardware reset path was broken for this target; software reset worked.
fix: Use 'pyocd reset -m sw' meanwhile; fixed in a later release.

title: Session open fails: 'SYS_AP_PSoC64' object has no attribute 'core'
symptoms: 'SYS_AP_PSoC64' object has no attribute 'core'
cause: GenericMemAPTarget lost its CoreSightCoreComponent base class in a refactor.
fix: Fixed by change #1350; update pyOCD.

title: i.MX RT mass erase prints 'Mass erase failed' although flash is erased
symptoms: E Mass erase failed. [eraser]
cause: The erase actually succeeded; the reported failure was a spurious message in 0.33.1 and the chosen reset type was not honoured by the target class.
fix: Verify by reading flash; the message is fixed in the next release.

title: 0.33.0: 'USB Error: Operation timed out' on pyocd list
symptoms: C USB Error: [Errno 10060] Operation timed out [__main__]
cause: Seen with the bundled libusb of 0.33.0 and some ST-Link probes; updating ST-Link firmware helped some users.
fix: Use 0.33.1 (which dropped the bundled libusb), update the probe firmware, check USB permissions or try another port or cable.

title: Picoprobe unreliable with pyocd (PC register not available)
symptoms: PC register is not available
cause: Probable signal-integrity trouble; the picoprobe optimizes by assuming target acknowledgements.
fix: Lower the SWD clock (-f 400000), try -Opicoprobe.safeswd=True, replug the probe, or use a CMSIS-DAP firmware on the Pico.

title: LPC55 factory-new chip: erase/flash fails after reset with memory transfer fault
symptoms: Core #0 is not accessible after reset
link exception during target disconnect: Memory transfer fault @ 0xe000edf0-0xe000edf3
cause: A new LPC55 starts with debug access locked; pyOCD unlocks it on connect but the reset done before flashing locks it again and the unlock was not repeated.
fix: Fixed in v0.33.0: the unlock is re-run after reset.

title: -f frequency option ignored with ST-Link V3
cause: A copy and paste bug stopped the requested SWD frequency from being applied; the probe itself only produces certain frequencies.
fix: Fixed on the develop branch (later release); measured actual clock may differ from requested because of ST-Link V3 prescalers.

title: nRF52 flash over CMSIS-DAP on macOS fails with DAP_TRANSFER response error
symptoms: DAP_TRANSFER response error
cause: Command packets arrived out of order or mixed up with a custom CMSIS-DAP firmware at high USB performance.
fix: Add -Ocmsis_dap.limit_packets (the =True form was broken until change #1259) and rebase the firmware on current DAPLink.

title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pyocd._version' when installed from source
symptoms: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pyocd._version
cause: pyocd._version is generated by setuptools_scm at build time, which setup.py does not install by itself.
fix: Install with 'pip install .' or install setuptools_scm[toml] first.

title: pyyaml version conflict between pyocd and cmsis-pack-manager
symptoms: ERROR: cmsis-pack-manager 0.4.0 has requirement pyyaml<7.0,>=6.0, but you'll have pyyaml 5.4.1 which is incompatible.
cause: pyOCD pinned pyyaml below 6.0 while newer cmsis-pack-manager required 6.0.
fix: Upgrade to pyOCD 0.32.1.

title: RP2040 over DAPLink probe: requires a probe with SWD sequence capability
symptoms: pyocd.core.exceptions.TargetSupportError: RP2040 requires a debug probe with SWD sequence capability
cause: RP2040 needs CMSIS-DAP commands added in protocol version 1.2.0; the probe runs older DAPLink firmware.
fix: Update the probe's DAPLink firmware to release 0254 or later.

title: PSoC 5LP kit with KitProg v1 is not detected
cause: That kit's programmer has no CMSIS-DAP mode, and pyOCD supports only KitProg2/3 in CMSIS-DAP mode; PSoC 5LP is not supported either.
fix: Use a vendor tool or a kit with KitProg3 or KitProg2 in CMSIS-DAP mode.

title: LPC55S28 flash fails with 'No ACK received'
symptoms: No ACK received
cause: The target was not responding to SWD; here one SWD pin had been reconfigured to another function in the application.
fix: Remove the pin mux for the SWD pins or recover the device (reset or erase) so the debug port is reachable.

title: Microchip nEDBG: 'DAP_CONNECT failed' with default protocol
symptoms: DAP_CONNECT failed
cause: The nEDBG probe did not respond properly to the default port selection.
fix: Connect with -O dap_protocol=swd. The device identity (variant) selected may also matter for actual programming.

title: STM32L475 built-in target has wrong DBGMCU register addresses
cause: A typo in the built-in target put the freeze registers at wrong addresses.
fix: Fixed by change #1193. For other STM32 parts use the CMSIS pack with a user script or debug sequences for DBGMCU.
